fullPassage:
Hello, first-year students. I'm your school counselor, Hannah Kim. How is your new school life? You may have experienced a situation where things didn't go as you expected at school. Have you ever wondered why this happens? Let's take a look at the following two cases.

The first case is about a student named Hajun. On the first day of school, Hajun's homeroom teacher introduced several school clubs. At that time, Hajun didn't have a particular preference for any of them. He thought that any indoor club would be okay since he was not an outdoor person. Can you guess what happened on the day of choice? He joined the soccer club. What made him choose soccer?

Well, a few days before submitting his application, he heard that the soccer club was so popular that half of his classmates were applying for it. This made him think that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club just because others did so. However, after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer was not for him. In the end, he regretted his decision.

Why do you think this happened? Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be excluded from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect." Following the crowd, of course, does not always lead to negative consequences, but it can lead to regret. So, how can you make your own choices? The first thing is to know what you really want. Although it might be different from your friends', don't be afraid to make your own choice. As long as you make the right choice for you, you will be happy about your decision.

Now, let's look at another case, one about Yubin. One day, Yubin told me about her first science quiz. Science was the subject that she struggled with the most. Since she wanted to get a good grade, she made a thorough study plan for herself. Yet, every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead. For instance, she cleaned her desk or texted her friends. These activities distracted her from studying, and in the end, she got a bad grade. She was frustrated that she continuously engaged in behaviors unhelpful for accomplishing her task.

When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in the short term. However, be careful! It could lead to repeated failures in certain tasks that you are not confident in doing.

If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually stop your self-handicapping.

As first-year students in high school, you'll sometimes face difficult moments. It is not unusual because everyone goes through difficult times. Even though you feel disappointed with your choices or behaviors, don't let yourself feel down. The most important thing is figuring out your own way to overcome your negative feelings. It will make your school life much more enjoyable. If you feel worried, remember that you are not alone. You have friends, teachers, and me. Good luck in this exciting new chapter of your life.

det.korean: 하준의 담임이 동아리를 소개했다. 지원서를 제출하기 며칠 전, 축구 동아리가 인기 있다는 것을 들었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① introduced: 과거시제. 정상.
✅ ② what: 간접의문문(guess what happened). 정상.
✅ ③ What: 의문대명사 주어(What made him). 정상.
❌ ④ submit → submitting: before + 동명사(before submitting). 전치사 뒤에 동명사 필요.
det.tip: before ~ing: ~하기 전에 / before는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사 / What made him choose: 무엇이 그로 하여금 ~하게 만들었는가

questions.passage: This made him think that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club just because others did so. However, after he ①<u>had joined</u> the club, he realized that soccer was not for him. Psychologists say that people ②<u>tend</u> to engage in certain behaviors just because others are ③<u>done</u> them. Also, people don't want to be excluded from ④<u>their</u> peers.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 동아리에 가입한 후 축구가 자신에게 맞지 않다는 것을 깨달았다. 사람들은 다른 사람들이 하고 있다는 이유만으로 특정 행동에 참여하는 경향이 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① had joined: 과거완료 — realized보다 앞선 시점. 정상.
✅ ② tend: people tend to (현재시제, 일반적 경향). 정상.
❌ ③ done → doing: 현재진행형(are doing). 다른 사람들이 '하고 있다'는 진행 의미.
✅ ④ their: people's peers. 소유격 정상.
det.tip: are doing(현재진행: 하고 있는) vs are done(수동완료: 끝난) / 과거완료(had + p.p.): 대과거

questions.passage: As first-year students in high school, you'll sometimes face difficult moments. It is not unusual because everyone goes through difficult times. det.analysis:
❌ ① disappointing → disappointed: 감정의 주체(you)가 '실망한' 상태이므로 과거분사. disappointing은 '실망시키는(감정 유발)'.
✅ ② feel: let yourself feel (사역동사 let + O + 동사원형). 정상.
✅ ③ figuring: The most important thing is figuring out (주격보어 동명사). 정상.
✅ ④ enjoyable: make ~ more enjoyable (형용사). 정상.
det.tip: disappointed(실망한, 감정 주체) vs disappointing(실망시키는, 감정 원인) / let + O + V원형

questions.passage: This made him think that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club just because others did so. However, after he had joined the club, he ①<u>realized</u> that soccer was not for him. In the end, he regretted his decision. Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be ②<u>excluded</u> from their peers. Following the crowd does not always lead to ④<u>favorable</u> consequences, but it can lead to regret.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 축구가 자신에게 맞지 않다는 것을 ①깨달았다. 또래에게서 ②배제되는 것을 원하지 않는다. 스스로 ③행동하기보다 군중을 따른다. 군중을 따르는 것이 항상 ④호의적인 결과를 초래하는 것은 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로 적절.
❌ ④ favorable(호의적인, 긍정적인) → 원문은 negative(부정적인). '부정적 결과를 항상 초래하는 것은 아니다'가 원문. favorable로 바꾸면 '긍정적 결과를 항상 초래하는 것은 아니다'로 의미가 완전히 달라짐.
⚠️ 함정: 'does not always'와 결합하면 favorable도 그럴듯해 보이지만, but it can lead to regret(후회로 이어질 수 있다)과 연결하면 부정적 결과가 맞음.
det.tip: negative(부정적인) ↔ favorable(호의적인, 긍정적인) / not always: 항상 ~은 아니다

questions.passage: Since she wanted to get a good grade, she made a thorough study plan for herself. det.korean: 과학에 ①집중하려 할 때마다 다른 일을 하게 되었다. 이 활동들은 공부에서 ②주의를 분산시켰다. 과제 수행에 도움이 되지 않는 행동에 지속적으로 ③참여했다. 자신감이 없으면 성공에 대한 ④기회를 만든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로 적절.
❌ ④ opportunities(기회) → 원문은 obstacles(장애물). 자신감이 없을 때 성공에 대한 '장애물'을 만드는 것이 자기 핸디캡핑. 기회를 만든다는 것은 정반대.
⚠️ 함정: ②distracted가 부정적이라 오답으로 보일 수 있으나, 원문 그대로 적절.
det.tip: obstacles(장애물) ↔ opportunities(기회) / create obstacles to success: 성공에 대한 장애물을 만들다

questions.passage: Well, a few days before submitting his application, he heard that the soccer club was so popular that half of his classmates were applying for it. questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 반 친구 절반이 지원한다는 것을 듣고 특별하다고 생각했다. 다른 사람들이 그렇게 했기 때문에 축구 동아리에 등록했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ others: 다른 사람들이 하니까 따라했다 = 편승 효과의 핵심.
❌ ① his teacher: 선생님이 했기 때문이라는 내용 없음.
❌ ② his parents: 부모 언급 없음.
❌ ④ nobody: 아무도 안 했다면 따라할 이유 없음.
det.tip: just because others did so: 다른 사람들이 그렇게 했기 때문에 / bandwagon effect의 핵심

questions.passage: If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually __________.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과정에 집중하면 압박감이 줄고 도전적 과제를 시도하게 된다. 이것이 결국 자기 핸디캡핑을 멈출 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② stop your self-handicapping: 과정 집중 → 압박 감소 → 도전 시도 → 자기 핸디캡핑 중단이라는 논리적 흐름.
❌ ① increase anxiety: 압박을 줄이는데 불안 증가는 모순.
❌ ③ worsen grades: 긍정적 변화 흐름에 성적 악화는 모순.
❌ ④ lower confidence: 격려받는 상황에서 자신감 저하는 모순.
det.tip: eventually: 결국 / Accordingly: 따라서 / ease the pressure: 압박 줄이기

✅ ③ 원문과 일치: didn't have a particular preference for any of them.
❌ ① 처음부터 좋아함: 선호 없었음.
❌ ② 야외 선호: was not an outdoor person.

ch: ② 자기 핸디캡핑은 자신감 있는 사람이 하는 행동이다.
③ 자기 핸디캡핑은 성공의 장애물을 만드는 행동이다.
④ 변명은 자존감을 낮추는 역할을 한다.

✅ ③ 원문 일치: create obstacles to success.
❌ ① 장기적 효과: 원문은 short term만 언급, However로 경고.

✅ ① 자기 핸디캡핑의 원인(자신감 부족, 결과 중시)과 해결 방법(과정 집중).

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 <u>These activities</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 예를 들어 책상을 치우거나 친구에게 문자를 보냈다. 이 활동들이 공부에서 주의를 분산시켰다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ These activities = 바로 앞 문장의 'cleaned her desk or texted her friends'.
❌ ① 과학 공부: 공부에서 '벗어난' 활동임.
❌ ② 계획 세우기: 계획은 이미 세웠고, 이것은 방해 활동.
❌ ④ 성적 확인/상담: 언급 없음.
det.tip: These/Those + 명사 = 바로 앞 문장의 구체적 내용을 지칭

questions.passage: Even though you feel disappointed with your choices or behaviors, don't let yourself feel down. You have friends, teachers, and <u>me</u>. Good luck in this exciting new chapter of your life.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 <u>me</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 걱정되면 혼자가 아니라는 것을 기억하라. 친구, 선생님, 그리고 나(상담사)가 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ me = 글의 화자인 학교 상담사 Hannah Kim. 첫 문단에서 'I'm your school counselor, Hannah Kim'이라고 자기 소개.
❌ ① 담임 선생님: 별도 인물.
❌ ② 과학 선생님: 언급 없음.
